You are the analyst of an unsupervised graph anomaly detection framework. You are given a label-free profile of an attributed graph and the catalog of applicable detection paradigms, each with the assumption it relies on. You do not know how the graph was built or what its anomalies look like; reason only from the evidence given. Select the small set of paradigms (1 to 4) whose assumptions the evidence supports, favouring complementary views over redundant ones. Reply with JSON only.

GRAPH PROFILE (label-free):
{
 "num_nodes": 11758,
 "num_edges": 1038000,
 "density": 0.015017,
 "avg_degree": 88.28,
 "max_degree": 2138,
 "degree_std": 161.82,
 "clustering_coeff": 0.5329,
 "num_communities": 26,
 "modularity": 0.5194,
 "homophily": 0.7492,
 "feature_dim": 10,
 "feature_sparsity": 0.4803,

 "spectral_gap": 0.132,
 "is_power_law": false
}

[
 {
  "name": "reconstruction",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes are hard to reconstruct from their neighborhood",
  "description": "Autoencoder-based: high reconstruction error \u2192 anomalous. Methods: DOMINANT, AnomalyDAE.",
  "applicable_because": "feature_dim = 10 satisfies >= 2"
 },
 {
  "name": "local_affinity",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes have low agreement with their neighbors",
  "description": "Neighbor feature similarity: low local affinity \u2192 anomalous. Methods: CoLA, SL-GAD.",
  "applicable_because": "homophily = 0.749 satisfies >= 0.3"
 },
 {
  "name": "contrastive",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes show low cross-view agreement",
  "description": "Multi-scale contrastive: low agreement across views \u2192 anomalous. Methods: ANEMONE, GRADATE.",
  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 50"
 },
 {
  "name": "adversarial",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes look fake to a discriminator",
  "description": "GAN-based: generator\u2013discriminator score as anomaly signal. Methods: GAAN.",
  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 500"
 },
 {
  "name": "one_class",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes fall outside the normal boundary in embedding space",
  "description": "SVDD on graph embeddings: distance from center \u2192 anomalous. Methods: OCGNN, DeepSAD.",
  "applicable_because": "feature_dim = 10 satisfies >= 2"
 },
 {
  "name": "density",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes lie in low-density regions of the embedding space",
  "description": "LOF/kNN in embedding space: low local density \u2192 anomalous.",
  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 30"
 },

  "applicable_because": "homophily = 0.749 satisfies >= 0.4"

  "name": "spectral",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes produce high-frequency signals on the graph",
  "description": "Graph wavelet / spectral response: high-frequency \u2192 anomalous.",
  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 30"
 },
 {
  "name": "attr_struct_mismatch",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes show divergence between attribute-based and structure-based rankings",
  "description": "Cross-modal rank divergence: attributes and structure disagree \u2192 anomalous.",
  "applicable_because": "feature_dim = 10 satisfies >= 2"
 },

  "name": "conformity",
  "assumption": "Anomalous actors hide behind template/minimal profiles \u2014 suspiciously conformant to the dominant feature pattern",
  "description": "Camouflage-by-conformity: NEGATIVE linear reconstruction residual. Only meaningful on template-dominated feature matrices (dup_rate >= 0.4), where anomalies are feature-space in-liers. Deterministic.",
  "applicable_because": "feature_dup_rate = 0.489 satisfies >= 0.4"
 }
]

response_content: {"selected_paradigms": ["attr_struct_mismatch", "conformity", "homophily_violation", "community"], "rationale": "attr_struct_mismatch shows the strongest landmarker separation (p99 0.914 vs p50 0.314, std 0.245), and the profile pairs rich structure (modularity 0.519, clustering_coeff 0.533, degree_std 161.8, 26 communities) with low-dimensional template features (feature_dim 10), so attribute-based and structure-based rankings can genuinely diverge. conformity is directly indicated by feature_dup_rate 0.489 and feature_sparsity 0.480: a template-dominated feature matrix where anomalies can camouflage as feature-space in-liers, a mechanism none of the tail-outlier paradigms capture; its saturated score distribution (p50 0.870) is itself consistent with that template dominance rather than a counter-signal. homophily_violation is reliable because homophily is high (0.749), making feature-neighbor mismatch discriminative, and its landmarker has a clean upper tail (p99 0.841, mean 0.387). community contributes a distinct structural-adherence view backed by strong modularity (0.519) and clustering (0.533) over 26 communities. density is excluded because its landmarker is effectively dead (p90 and p95 both 0.0), and reconstruction/one-class are dropped as redundant and weak on a 10-dimensional template feature space already covered by the selected complementary views."}
